articleTitle: Simulation of multiphase induction heating systems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Multiphase induction heating systems have particular features which make them attractive for application to some heating and melting processes in industry. Among the advantages is the possibility of heating quite uniformly, limited regions of a body without moving the inductor above its surface, the reduction of the vibrations of an inductor and load due to the electrodynamic forces and hence the noise produced by them, and the provision of a nearly balanced three phase load of a power network. These advantages may be achieved in the best manner by the so called "travelling wave induction heating" (TWIH). The authors present a simulation and study of some the peculiar characteristics of this type of inductors. Particular attention is paid to the simulation of TWIH systems for heating thin cylindrical and plain bodies including transverse flux heating.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel implementations of the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper different parallel and sequential implementations of the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method are evaluated. The performance of current sequential architectures are first investigated. Possible improved performances from different parallel architectures are then examined. The parallel implementations consist of a network of workstations, a transputer network and an implementation on a single instruction stream multiple data stream (SIMD) architecture. The FDTD algorithm, a discretisation of Maxwell's curl equations used to solve electromagnetic boundary value problems is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of dynamical behaviours of electro-magneto-mechanical coupled systems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents three coupling models for analysing the dynamical behaviour of a coupled electro-magneto-mechanical system. The first is based on the parametrization of the system by the finite element method. The second realizes the coupling by solving alternately the electromagnetic equations to get the force and mechanical equations to derive the motion. The third solves simultaneously the electric circuit, magnetic field and mechanical motion equations. A comparison of the three models is given through the modelling of an electromagnetic actuator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Three dimensional cylindrical coordinate finite-difference time-domain analysis of curved slotline
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A curved slotline is analyzed in three dimensional cylindrical coordinates using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. A modified dispersive boundary condition is utilized in the computation which alleviates the instability problem associated with the conventional dispersive boundary condition. This improves the accuracy of the results greatly. Computational results for the slotline dispersion characteristics of different substrates, slot-widths and radii are presented, discussed and compared with those obtained from closed form formulas for a straight slotline.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast algorithm for the wideband analysis of 3-D waveguide junctions
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A new algorithm for the wideband analysis of arbitrarily shaped 3-D waveguide junctions is briefly described. Using a special full-wave method, the algorithm determines the poles and the residues of the y-matrix directly, thus permitting to obtain the representation of the circuit in the whole band of interest and avoiding time-consuming frequency-by-frequency field computations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An advanced algorithm for transient analysis of grounding systems by moments method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: An advanced numerical algorithm for transient analysis of grounding systems based on moments method in frequency domain is presented. Electrical symmetries of the structure are considered in order to reduce the computational effort. The algorithm implementation is organized to exploit the architectural features of vector and parallel computational environments. The computer performances obtained by running some large size examples are illustrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The simulation of coupled electromagnetic and thermal problems in microwave heating
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Microwaves are used for the thermal processing of various materials such as food and ceramics. They differ from conventional heating methods where heat input is on the material surface only, in that heat power may be delivered virtually anywhere inside the volume of the material. Thus, heating with microwaves opens new possibilities such as faster processing, more precise delivery of heat power and localised heating at specific areas. The aim of this paper is to describe the modelling concepts for combined electromagnetic and thermal problems from the point of view of the transmission-line modelling (TLM) method. Typical results of simulations are also included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 2-D numerical simulation of electrostatic micrometer torque
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The mathematical model of an electrostatic position microactuator is formulated. Both circuit and 2-D field models are presented and discussed. The micromotor is investigated at steady state under various supply conditions and considering different materials, for a given device geometry. The torque-angle curve is calculated, as well as the electric field distribution along the air gap; design considerations are accordingly drawn.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analytical modelling of frequency parameters of lines
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: In many analyses of line parameters, approximations ignoring eddy currents in conductors can be used. But, in close conductors, the AC parameters vary greatly with frequency and conductor spacing. For some configurations, the increase in resistance due to skin and proximity effects can be in excess of 100% compared to skin effect resistance alone. The present paper deals with the analytical calculation of per unit length impedances of closely parallel multiwire lines in a frequency range covering (0 Hz, 5 MHz).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mutual impedance and the folded dipole
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper combines the induced-EMF method of determining the mutual impedance between two dipoles and the transmission line model of the folded dipole in order to develop an expression for the mutual impedance between a dipole and a folded dipole; and between two dipoles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of antenna mutual coupling from radiated far fields
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Mutual coupling between a pair of identical array elements is calculated from the radiated far field. The mutual coupling is found by using the reaction theorem applied to a single element. Different reaction surfaces are considered and results are compared to the conventional near and far field aperture surface integration technique. Results of the far field reaction technique are given for both a Hertzian dipole and waveguide aperture model. The results clearly show increased accuracy when compared with conventional aperture surface calculations using far fields. The method is believed to provide a quick and easy estimate of the mutual coupling from the measured far field data of a single array element. The technique is intended to be used as a development tool for the design of phased array elements with low mutual coupling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design optimisation using the BEM coupled with genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Presents optimisation in electrostatics using the boundary element method (BEM) coupled with a genetic algorithm (GA). In the first part, the boundary element method is briefly introduced. This method is a powerful tool which is characterised by very high accuracy, only the boundaries of the investigated domain must be discretised. In the second part, the genetic algorithm to solve the optimisation problems is described. The third part is dedicated to explain the way the two methods are coupled together. Finally, the fourth part provides two analytical examples to illustrate the GA in actual terms and an insulator is optimised to illustrate the solution of a real problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of travelling electric field manipulation of bioparticles
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The authors theoretically simulate the travelling wave dielectrophoresis phenomena observed by Huang et al. (1993). Such simulations can be used to design electrode geometries and determine the experimental conditions for facilitating such effects as the selective separation of cells from heterogeneous populations. The authors use the method of moments and the finite element method. Of the two techniques, the finite element method is the most computationally efficient and flexible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of electromagnetic devices using sensitivities computed with the adjoint variable method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The adjoint variable method allows the sensitivities with respect to all system parameters to be computed at the cost of a solution to an adjoint problem. The present paper derives expressions for the sensitivities in terms of the fields of the original and the adjoint problems. Expressions for the sources to the adjoint problem are also derived. These expressions are then applied to an example in which the objective is to maximize the levitating force on a conducting ring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generalized BIE-BLA formulation of skin and proximity effect problems for an arbitrary regime of the magnetic field generation
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper presents a new boundary element formulation for skin and proximity effect problems of parallel conductors. The main idea of this formulation is the representation of the functions for which the solution is sought in the form of two sequential approximations, the zero-order approximation giving the solution of the problem in the high frequency limit and the first-order approximation describing the correction of the order boundary layer approximation. Unlike the BIE-IBC formulations used presently, the integral equations for the expansion coefficients allow one to separate the unknown variables into "time-dependent" and "space-dependent" components for electromagnetic pulses of an arbitrary form as well as for a harmonic field. The final form of the integral equations for the "space-dependent" components is independent of the parameters of the magnetic field generation regime and is defined solely by the geometrical parameters of the conductor system under consideration. The formulation is developed for E-H and A-Y formalisms independently, but the resulting integral equations are the same for both formalisms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generation of an optimal reluctance network model for fast 2-D and 3-D simulations of electromagnetic devices
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The reluctance network method (RNM) is one of the numerical methods that allow computation of magnetic fields in different electromagnetic devices. In this method the analysed space is replaced by a network of magnetic reluctances, with magnetomotive forces as supply sources. It allows one to analyse magnetic fields in two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) domains, Turowski et al. (1990), and in comparison to other numerical methods (e.g. finite-element) the calculation time is much shorter, with accuracy sufficient in most cases of engineering CAD. The factors that influence the accuracy of the RNM modelling are discussed. The procedure of obtaining an optimal RNM model is described, using the example of a quasi-3D model of a linear oscillating motor, Mendrela and Pudlowski (1992). The generated RNM model allows one to calculate accurately magnetic fields, coil inductance and forces in the motor in a very short time, Worotynski et al. (1993), even on a personal computer. Computation results are compared with the measured ones.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of multilayered semiconductor leaky rib waveguides
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Presents an easy to implement, accurate, two dimensional simulation of a leaky rib waveguide using the discrete spectral index method. The results obtained clearly indicate that the nature of the radiation losses encountered in leaky rib waveguides can be exploited to engineer a structure that has the modal benefits of being essentially single moded at dimensions considerably larger than those of a similar rib waveguide based upon a low refractive index substrate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dispersion of time-domain and frequency-domain formulations of the symmetrical condensed TLM node
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The dispersion characteristics of the 3-D symmetrical condensed TLM node are analysed. New results are given for the stub-less frequency-domain node and the stub-loaded time-domain node.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Permanent magnet modelling by edge element and facet element (discussion on the force distribution in permanent magnet)
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The permanent magnet is modeled by two dual formulations (h-oriented and b-oriented formulations) by using respectively edge element and facet element in three dimensions. The virtual work principle is applied for the force calculation in the permanent magnet. The calculation of local forces is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of graded and multigrid techniques in transmission-line modelling
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The transmission-line modelling (TLM) method of numerical electromagnetic analysis with the symmetrical condensed node is well established. However, in many systems there is the need to represent very fine features within large volumes and, in 3-dimensions, it is rarely possible to employ a uniform mesh throughout the entire problem space. The traditional approach to this problem is to use a graded mesh. The stub-loaded node was originally used but more recently a hybrid node has been developed which requires fewer stubs. The disadvantage of using a graded mesh is that fine regions cannot be completely localised and there is an upper limit on the timestep which is determined by the smallest node dimensions. In an alternative approach, termed the multigrid method, the principles of connectivity and synchronism are relaxed so that regions of different spatial and temporal resolution can be joined together to form a complete system. Useful work can be done if each region consists of uniform cubic nodes but, in general, each region can be considered as a separate graded mesh. The transfer of information between different regions cannot be exact but good results can be obtained with significant reductions in both run-time and storage. If it is assumed that a uniform mesh cannot be used then the choice is between using a single graded mesh or a multigrid mesh. If the multigrid approach is adopted then there is a choice of using cubic nodes or graded mesh regions and if cubic nodes are selected it may be possible to use a node without stubs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advances in neural network non-destructive testing
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A neural system architecture based on a concept of task decomposition, and capable of handling fuzzy variables, aimed to treat nondestructive testing applications is described. To demonstrate the efficiency of this approach an electrostatic sample problem is presented and adequately solved. However, the techniques discussed are of general applicability, and then suitable for practical NDT problems. Special emphasis is placed on the analysis of the manner in which a simple neural network extracts useful information about the problem via the learning process. Starting from this analysis a strategy of decomposition is derived and successfully applied to the test problem. One of the key features of the proposed model is that the performance of the whole system can easily be improved by locating the problematic portions, whereas an ordinary neural network model acts as a black box.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved modelling of head-antenna interactions using spherical wave expansions
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper uses a simple spherical model for the head and makes a number of promising comparisons of predicted and observed azimuth patterns of a handset operating close to the head. Also included is an experimental verification of the program using a truly spherical and homogeneous scatterer. The paper describes the following improvements and extensions of this technique: (1) a two layer model of the head is incorporated; (2) results are obtained both for a half-wave dipole, where previously a Hertzian dipole was assumed; (3) simple arrays of elements are also treated; and (4) near field and internal field patterns are produced, with improved graphics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FDTD modelling of 3D optical pulse propagation in linear and nonlinear materials
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The modelling of 3D optical pulse propagation in linear materials using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is discussed. A full 3D formulation run on a massively parallel processor and a body of revolution formulation are described and results presented for the interaction of a Gaussian beam with a linear thin lens. The extension of the method to include nonlinear effects is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new vision of numerical methods for the solution of Maxwell's equations related to the FD-TD method; application to general anisotropic media
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Some proposals of numerical methods of solution of Maxwell's equations have appeared in which different meshes and orders of approximation have been used. The relation between finite difference and finite volume has also been pointed out. In this paper a complementary point of view is proposed by the use of the general Stokes' theorem to express Faraday's and Ampere's laws as volume-surface equations. Isotropic materials are treated first, then an application to anisotropic media is introduced through an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An impedance UTD model for the prediction of terrain undulation and roughness effects in radiating systems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A feasibility study of evaluating the terrain effects on radiating systems using analytical and computational techniques is presented. The problem of site effect evaluation is divided into three stages: terrain modelling, ray tracing and field evaluation. Innovative techniques are introduced at each stage to make the model versatile enough to handle most general terrain contours and also reduce computational requirements to a minimum. The result is a scheme that can evaluate most terrain types on a mini/micro computer. The model developed is applied to study the site effects on two important electromagnetic systems for navigation and position location: the instrument landing system (ILS) and the microwave landing system (MLS). A summary of results for actual sites is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved physical basis for computer modelling of radiation from curved wires
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The determination of the behaviour of a wire antenna in a known impressed field is a fundamental problem of applied electromagnetics. The authors propose a moment method using polynomial and finite trigonometric series basis functions which gives reasonable and stable results even with very closely spaced parallel wires. The results are in general agreement with those of Smith (1972) (who analysed a somewhat different structure). It was found that the variations of the surface current distribution over the wire antenna are heavily dependent on the average current flowing into the wire and the method of coupling to the antenna. The modelling of surface current distribution in such detail is essential for highly-resonant structures dominated by conductor loss, such as superconducting antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical modelling of diffraction by objects in GTEM cell
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The GTEM (GigaTEM) cell is proving a useful tool for simulating free space scattering of objects under laboratory conditions. The authors present an efficient numerical algorithm for the characterization of the discontinuities presented by perfectly conducting cubic or spherical objects. Numerical results are compared with experimental data (provided by EMC Baden), showing very good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental verification of a finite element solution to heating problems in a multi-mode cavity
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Computational analysis is playing an increasingly important part in the design process for microwave applicators and packaging of food products. It is important to assess these methods with respect to real situations and experimental results rather than simply testing the method on a problem for which the analytical solution is known. These test problems rarely reflect the complexities of a real heating problem, such as where a dielectric material load is placed in a multimode microwave applicator. To reflect realistic heating the authors have used a resonant cavity of a similar size to a typical domestic oven and a food material, mashed potato. They have also carried out tests on a block of low loss plastic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A TLM algorithm simulator for the visualization of time discrete electromagnetic processes
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Describes a transmission line matrix (TLM) algorithm simulator which has been specifically designed as an educational computer tool for visualizing the numerical TLM process of electromagnetic field propagation. Unlike traditional time domain electromagnetic field simulators which compute and display the overall (macroscopic) field in space and time, this simulator visualizes the scattering and spreading of the individual (microscopic) voltage impulses in the TLM mesh, thus allowing the student to observe all the scattering events simultaneously in time, and in parallel in space, as well as to integrate the elementary scattering processes into a global electromagnetic field function. In addition, the algorithm simulator provides insight into the numerical dispersion, anisotropy of propagation constant, and spurious modes in discrete field models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Steady-state characteristics of a shaded-pole motor by finite element analysis
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The authors model only one pole pitch of a shaded-pole motor, exploiting the inherent periodicity of the boundary conditions. Excitation for the model is derived directly from the applied stator voltage which is not restricted to any particular time variation. Rotor motion is simulated by moving one pole pitch of the rotor in discrete spatial steps and tying this movement to the time step used in the discretisation of the excitation voltage waveform. At each time step and rotor position the field solution is coupled to the external electrical circuit and the current is determined taking magnetic nonlinearity of the permeable regions into account. Continuous motion of the rotor is simulated by returning the rotor to its starting position after movement through one pole pitch. The technique does not require expensive preprocessing after each rotor position. Any general purpose pre-processor can be used to generate the model in the usual way. Additional reorganisation of the input data structure is carried out within the solver code once only.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite element modelling of magnetic fields and calculation of static characteristics of linear step motors for control rod drives of nuclear reactors
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Describes an accurate method for the calculation of the static characteristics of linear step motors (LSMs) used as actuators in control rod drives of nuclear reactors. By static characteristics, the authors mean the electromagnetic force developed by the motor versus armature displacement curve that determines motor performance in its standing and dynamic modes of operation. The method is based on the modelling and computation of nonlinear axisymmetric magnetic fields in the LSM using the finite element technique. Some of the simulation results are compared with available experimental data which validates the developed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interfacing the transmission line method (TLM) and state-space (SS) techniques to analyse general non-linear structures
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper describes a technique for analysing general electromagnetic structures including distributed regions and lumped non-linear sub-circuits, employing the transmission-line-matrix and the state space method. The analysis is entirely performed in the time domain. The technique took advantage of each of the methods and offers a wide range of applications especially for the analysis of general electromagnetic structures at high frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A recursive FE-TD algorithm for the analysis of the interaction between an EM field and a lossy multiconductor line
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents an efficient algorithm for the time domain analysis of the interaction of an electromagnetic field with a lossy multiconductor line. Inclusion of loss in interaction problems leads to convolution integrals whose computation needs heavy computer times. The algorithm utilized in this paper is based on a recursive formulation for the evaluation of the convolution integrals allowed by the exponential form of the kernel. The solution of the transient equations is achieved by means of the finite element method. New expressions for the transient parameters associated to the influence of the lossy ground on the coupling analysis are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hybrid time domain modelling for automotive EMC
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The transmission line modelling-time domain integral equation (TLM-TDIE) technique is introduced. A comparison between three modelling methods, TLM-TDIE, hybrid symmetrical condensed node TLM and multigrid TLM is presented. The application of numerical modelling to automotive electromagnetic compatibility design is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The mathematical methods and electromagnetic codes for a physical electronics devices
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Describes algorithms and codes of the CAD system TOPAZ that have been extensively used in the practical design of a variety of instruments and devices. The modern engineering design of physical electronics devices is not possible without the use of powerful mathematical methods and CAD software. The TOPAZ system is a combination of mathematical software, system and application programs meant for the functional design of a variety instruments and devices for electronics and RF-electrodynamics. The software includes a variety of original methods and algorithms for calculating 2D and 3D physical fields of various types, and methods and algorithms for simulation of the electron optical problems of high current beams, precision optics of imaging electron optical systems, electrodynamics etc. The codes can be used to solve the design problems, such as, analysis, optimisation and synthesis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analytical and new transmission line equivalent circuit modelling methods for swept frequency of power transformers
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The technique of swept frequency response for condition monitoring of power transformers in-situ provides a non-intrusive means of determining the mechanical integrity of winding systems. The paper describes a new modelling strategy by which the physical dimensions, electromagnetic field distribution, and material properties of the transformer construction are fed into a purpose written program which generates an equivalent circuit model for the windings. The circuit model would be suitable for solution by standard network solvers such as SPICE. A comparison between the measured and calculated results using the newly developed technique for frequency response tests are encouraging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computations of superconducting magnet's quench processes
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Superconducting magnets applied in magnetic separators produce large magnetic fields. They can work nominally at elevated direct currents in steady states. A superconducting winding has zero electrical resistance at a temperature of 4.2 K. Sometimes, because of local disturbances, e.g. local mechanical or thermal stresses or rise in magnetic field, the winding becomes a resistive one and energy dissipation raises its temperature. A quench (superconductivity loss) in the coil can lead to an immense magnetic field energy discharge. The averaged critical parameters of the cryomagnet winding have been applied so far to analyze and design cryomagnets. The in-time variability of these parameters has not been usually considered. A new two-dimensional numerical model of the resistive zone propagation in the superconducting winding is developed. In the quench analysis not only the circuit electrical parameters such as resistance and inductance, but also the instantaneous local superconductor critical parameters, which are decisive for a transition of any winding point to a resistive state, are taken into account.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel adaptive generator based on Kohonen's neural network model and vector quantization
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Using a novel way to realize adaptive mesh generation, the authors take advantage of the asymptotic Voronoi partition and dual Delaunay triangulation property of SOM/LVQ and VQ, and drive the potential mesh generator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Exact operator method for the analysis of dielectric waveguides with application to integrated optics devices and laser facets
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A rigorous implementation of Fourier operators is applied to the analysis of open dielectric waveguide devices. The method is exact and easily implemented using readily available numerical techniques. The method is applied to two problems of practical interest in integrated optics: (1) the analysis of reflection and transmission at a general slab waveguide discontinuity or as a special case, a laser facet; and (2) the scalar analysis of a rib waveguide. The solution is exact and a polarisation correction may be applied to yield polarised mode propagation constants.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discontinuities in planar millimeter circuits by FD-TD method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The successful application of FD-TD methods to millimetric planar transmission lines presupposes a satisfactory answer to the problem of infinite line termination absorbing boundary condition (ABC) in presence of high frequency dispersion. It is the purpose of this work to evaluate the efficiency of some commonly employed ABCs and to present a technique that reduces reflection error to less than 1% for microstrip and coplanar line circuits up to and beyond 50 GHz, that is lower than the discretization and round-off errors introduced by the FD-TD technique. The authors report some examples of microstrip and coplanar line circuits, comparing results with those obtained by other authors as well as with those of commercial packages and with experimental data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite difference analysis of active optical waveguide devices
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: It is shown that a finite difference method for numerically determining the propagation characteristics of optical waveguide devices can be extended to deal with structures containing complex refractive indices in a straightforward manner. The resulting complex finite difference method has been validated and its potential as a design tool demonstrated with studies of a silicon based p-i-n optical rib waveguide modulator and a semiconductor laser.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A numerical calculation of transient antenna impedance
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The authors describe a time-domain approach to the determination of transient antenna impedance. The antenna is treated as a scattering surface subject to a strongly localised electric field. This incident field is set uniformly to zero, except in the region of the feed where it is defined such that an effective voltage is apparent. Surface currents can then be computed for the antenna, using a marching-in-time method based on a solution of the electric field integral equation (EFIE). The defined source voltage and computed feed current can then be used to determine the input impedance of the antenna over a very wide band, via the Fourier transform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical prediction of three-dimensional temperature distributions inside a microwave oven using the method of lines
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The method of lines, a variant of the finite difference time domain technique, is used to transform Maxwell's equations into a set of ordinary differential equations for the electromagnetic fields within a microwave oven loaded with a composite dielectric material. The power density is then derived and used to calculate the temperature field. The effects of external controls, e.g. a turntable, are modelled and the implications discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A moment method analysis of a transverse slot fed by a boxed stripline
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A moment method analysis of a slot radiator excited by means of a boxed stripline configuration has been developed. The method employs entire domain basis functions to optimise computational efficiency and the results obtained are generally in good agreement with measurement and with the theoretical predictions of other contributors. This is particularly true for the more practical, strongly coupled, configurations for which the strip feed line lies entirely under the slot radiator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of a D-band quarterwave microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Describes the steps taken to model a quarter wave microstrip antenna. The design is well established and has received recent attention for its potential use as a receiving antenna for cellular telephones and paging devices. The commercial finite element software MSC/EMAS was used for this study.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of domain decomposition methods for numerical modeling of wave phenomena on serial and parallel computer architectures
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Domain decomposition has significant potential for analyzing large problems. By partitioning a problem into logical blocks, repetition can be avoided and efficiency can be increased. The most applicable solution technique can be used for each block without regard to the behavior in other blocks. Large and complex structures can be conveniently analyzed piecewise. Domain decomposition is well suited for massively parallel processing, although special consideration is necessary to maximize the efficiency. The technique demonstrates that elementary tasks such as boundary value problems can be solved in new ways that take full advantage of parallelism. The paper explains the basics of the technique, and gives a few examples of its application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Moment method of computing equivalent circuit of coplanar waveguide T-junction
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: For some of its advantages, the coplanar waveguide (CPW) is preferred to the microstrip line in developing monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs). However, due to lack of powerful design software, the potentials of this line have not been fully exploited. This paper introduces a computer technique for the determination of the equivalent circuit of the CPW T-junction. It can be extended to find the equivalent circuits of CPW bends, terminations, steps etc. The technique is based on the assumption of the quasi-TEM wave propagation in the CPW structure. The electric and magnetic fields around the junction are derived from electric and magnetic potentials which are the solutions of the Laplace equation. These solutions are achieved using the spectral domain formulation in conjunction with the moment method. Results presented include the equivalent circuit of a T-junction which was evaluated in order to find its scattering parameters when the junction is shorted at one of its ports. These parameters are compared with those obtained by an electromagnetic simulator, and with those measured.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 2D finite element/boundary element method applied to practical 2D and 3D scattering problems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The finite element/boundary element (FE/BE) method for solving electromagnetic (EM) problems has been investigated and implemented. A careful validation of the method (using both canonical problems that can be computed analytically and measured data from complex real-world problems) has been performed. The FE/BE has been applied to otherwise intractable and important problems in RCS reduction evaluations. Line source radiation close to human beings as well as power dissipated in humans near line sources has also been considered using the FE/BE method. Some adaptive finite element methods used to improve the computational efficiency of the FE/BE method are being investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method to improve computation efficiency for the radiation pattern of an airborne antenna
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The authors propose a technique to improve the computation efficiency for an airborne antenna pattern by reducing the number of computation terms. In order to do that, an algorithm is presented for evaluating the contribution of each ray path to the total pattern and for searching for dominant terms. As a criterion of this evaluation, they have noted that the field incident on each edge which becomes a diffracted field. The field strength propagating along each ray path is also checked to find the dominant terms. A small twin engine aircraft is employed as an example of applying the evaluation method. The radiation pattern of an antenna mounted on the aircraft has been calculated by their algorithm. The pattern obtained by the conventional UTD analysis is also presented, in which many computation terms including dominant and minor terms are integrated. The patterns presented by these methods are compared to test the accuracy and computation efficiency of their method. Measurement is also made using a scale model aircraft in order to check the accuracy of the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient computer modelling of interaction of field and surface crack in surface magnetic field measurement technique
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A computer technique for an efficient analysis of surface electromagnetic field distributions induced by U-shaped current-carrying wires and rectangular coils around fatigue cracks in ferrous metals was presented. The technique employs the unfolding method in conjunction with a bipolar conformal mapping in order to reduce the problem to a 2-D Laplace equation subject to appropriate boundary conditions. This equation is solved using a fast Fourier transform. Computed results were presented and where possible, the accuracy of the technique was verified by measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dimensioning and design of direct controlled solenoid actuators in cryogenic Ariane 5 valves
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: In the Ariane 5 launcher several cryogenic valve actuation units are required, e.g. the helium supply system and the tank pressurization system. The technical specifications demand for fast acting actuators under various constraints such as temperature conditions, low mass, minimum power demand and reliability; the temperatures range from about 420 K over ambient to cryogenic, liquid hydrogen (20 K) or liquid helium (2.8 K). These requirements are met by the design of direct controlled solenoid actuators. The development of the actual design and layout is backed computationally and verified by tests. Modeling of the (electro-)magnetic circuit including permanent magnet, solenoids and several air gaps is needed for design purposes in order to yield sufficient force margins for the operation of the actuator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The imagist's wand
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper explores the role of computer imagery as an aid to the early understanding of key concepts in the presentation of field theory and related topics. It draws upon the use of simple and highly visual programs developed for the transfer of specific concepts in support of both undergraduate and post graduate teaching at Plymouth. Some of the methods used to enhance the learning process in a selection of programs are presented. Excellent results are obtained with only a modest outlay and non specialist programming skills.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of steady-state characteristics of a single-phase shaded pole induction motor by circuit-field method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A circuit-field combined method is described with reference to the steady-state characteristics evaluation of a single-phase shaded pole induction motor. Saturation of iron core, asymmetry of structure and heterogeneity of materials are taken into account. The circuit and potential equations, electromagnetic parameters and the manner of solution of the equations for sinusoidal approximation are determined. The calculated mechanical and electromechanical characteristics of the test motor were compared with measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field method of performance characteristics shaping of electrical machine by construction modifications
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The field model for the calculation of the torque-speed characteristics of the industrial type d.c. motor PXOVKf 104b-2 is presented. The 2D FEM method is used. The influence of the magnetization level of the magnetic circuit as well as the properties of the magnetic constructional materials on the shape of torque-speed characteristics are analyzed. Finally, the possibilities of motor construction modifications, from the point of view of the required shape of this characteristic, are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Beam optimization by means of a reconfigurable reflector with true bending stiffness
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes a new approach to realize a reconfigurable surface with true bending stiffness. The reflector surface consists of a mesh of interwoven flexible wires. The goal is to realize a space antenna with a dynamically controlled footprint (e.g. zoom capability), using a minimum of control points.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate modelling of IC interconnect performance using the method of lines
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The accurate electrical modelling of integrated circuit (IC) interconnects is important to enable simulation of microwave devices and circuits to be possible. At present the electrical properties, at high frequencies, of IC interconnects are not accurately obtainable by RF on wafer probing. A modified "method of lines" (MoL) electromagnetic field simulator has been devised to extract the required electrical parameters given the physical dimensions and properties of the substrate and conductors. The technique accurately accounts for substrate and conductor losses, multi-stripline structures, and allows the stacking, vertically, of conductors within the substrate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate and efficient representations of exact electromagnetic scattering models using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: An efficient method to accurately model electromagnetic scattering based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) is described. Adaptive ANNs are utilised as approximators to model reflection from a lossless dielectric slab and scattering from a sphere. Correspondence to Mie scattering is achieved to within a normalised RMS error of 1.9%. Applications to the modelling of scattering from particle distributions are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computational aspects of shortwave scattering by a smooth waveshaped grating under grazing incidence
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The authors consider the following time-harmonic problem: a smooth waveshaped periodic boundary is illuminated by a plane electromagnetic wave. The surface is assumed to be perfectly conductive and the problem is treated in two dimensional case, so it can be separated in two scalar problems for E and H polarization. Therefore the wave field as a scalar function satisfies the reduced wave equation and Dirichlet's or Neumann's boundary condition according to polarization. All the numerical results presented hold for the case of Dirichlet's boundary condition, although the asymptotic formulae can be extended to other boundary conditions. The problem is investigated under the following assumptions: i) wavelength of the incident plane wave is assumed to be small compared with the period of the boundary, height of the humps, and radius of curvature of the boundary. This means the shortwave approximation applies and both ideas and methods of the GTD can be used. ii) The grazing angle is small. This implies that only the tops of the humps of the boundary are illuminated while all other parts of the boundary remain unlit, i.e. in a deep shadow. Both these assumptions seem to be natural for the problem of radiolocation near the ocean surface. The latter one has attracted the authors' attention and remains the main aim of their investigations. In present formulation the authors model the ocean surface as a wavy periodic boundary and reduce the problem to the 2D case. Thus they arrive at the classical problem of the grating theory which nevertheless can be regarded as the model one for the problem mentioned above.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization and modelling of electrically small systems to predict EMC performance in different environments
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The use of numerical modelling tools to simulate the behaviour of practical electronic equipment is only usually possible if simplifications are made to the system. Often this results in the modelling of stylized equipment, which is not desirable. A promising method to overcome this is to determine, through measurements, the fundamental radiation parameters of such systems and use these parameters directly in the modelling method. The present paper describes such an approach. An electrically small test device is decomposed into its equivalent electric and magnetic dipoles which are then used in simulations. The simulation method used is transmission-line modelling (TLM) and the equivalent dipole representation of the equipment, and subsequent modelling, is validated against experimental results with a close agreement between the two.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An equivalent electric network model for nonlinear 3-D magnetostatic field analysis
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: An equivalent electric network model for nonlinear magnetostatic field analysis is presented. The electric circuit allows a simple analysis of the magnetic field distribution in the presence of homogeneous and inhomogeneous materials and allows an easy linkage of lumped parameter circuits and field equations. The model can be used for the analysis of direct and inverse problems, furthermore, an estimate of the B-H curve of a nonlinear material can be obtained. The method has been tested comparing the calculated results with linear and nonlinear benchmark problems. Then the characteristics of the method are shown analysing the magnetic field due to an electromagnet with a large air gap.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical calculation of the temperature distribution in the melt of induction crucible furnaces
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: In induction furnaces, power losses from the eddy currents in the melt are used to heat the charged metal. Nearly all of the induced heating power is generated inside the melt within the small depth of penetration. On the other hand, the electromagnetic Lorentz forces on the molten metal cause heat transport by forced convection. The question is wether the influence of convection is strong enough to homogenize the temperature of the melt. This paper deals with a method to calculate numerically the steady state temperature distribution within the melt, taking into account the heat transport by conduction, convection and radiation. The calculations were done for a 800 kg steel furnace with a filling level of 125 %, an induced power of 50 kW at 500 Hz; any other combinations can be calculated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The finite-element modelling of three-dimensional time-harmonic electromagnetic fields
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: An efficient and accurate finite-element method is presented for computing time-harmonic electromagnetic fields in three-dimensional configurations containing arbitrarily inhomogeneous media that may be anisotropic. To obtain accurate results with an optimum computational efficiency, both consistently linear edge and consistently linear nodal elements are used for approximating the spatial distribution of the field. In comparison with earlier work, the formulation is improved by adding methods for the explicit modelling of the electromagnetic compatibility relations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A computational study of localised loss in a distribution transformer
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The localised loss in a 1000 kVA distribution transformer core model has been computed with the aid of a 386 microprocessor based personal computer using novel software. Overall core loss in the transformer model has been computed to be 1371 W at core flux density of 1.6 T. The loss measured in a commercial transformer core of similar geometry and rating was 1299 W thus giving a discrepancy of 5.6%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applying 3-D FEM to evaluate induction heating of a slab
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: To evaluate the performance of induction heating of a conducting and permeable slowly moving slab including the distribution of the eddy current field and the temperature in the 3D space, the finite element method (FEM) is applied. The calculation is consistent with experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An entire domain analysis of a horizontally polarized omnidirectional antenna array
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: An entire domain analysis of an omnidirectional linear array antenna, in which the radiating elements are slot doublets in a rectangular waveguide, has been developed. A numerical example is presented to verify the validity of the proposed formulation. The numerical results are in good agreement with measurement and consequently the resultant computer program represents accurate design tool for omnidirectional arrays comprising of a shunt slot pair in a rectangular waveguide.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computation of 3-D capacitances of transmission line discontinuities with the boundary element method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: With increasing clock rates and scale of integration in microelectronics and PCB-design problems, electromagnetic compatibility achieve more and more importance. Especially since problems of transmission line discontinuities occur during the design process of electronic devices. For an accurate simulation of the circuit model and signal behaviour before the production process, information is needed about transmission line discontinuities which occur as parasitic elements in order to save time and costs for redesign, which is necessary if malfunction arises due to problems of EMC. In this paper attention is focused on the capacitance values of three-dimensional structures which appear as transmission line discontinuities. For this case the method of boundary elements can be applied. The authors have developed a method of calculating the capacitance value of full three-dimensional structures like via's, connectors and cross-overs using the indirect boundary element method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of the dynamic performance of non-linear electro-mechanical systems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A coupled transient finite element/system simulation technique is applied to the analysis of a nonlinear electro-mechanical actuation system. It facilitates the investigation of alternative control strategies for an application in which performance analysis in the time domain is important to the design optimization process. The technique permits the modelling of all the multi-disciplinary facets of the problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite difference modelling of non-linear behavior in high temperature superconducting transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A two dimensional finite difference analysis of high temperature superconducting (HTS) strip transmission lines is presented. In particular, the nonlinear response of the HTS striplines to high RF currents is modelled. The anisotropic Ginzburg-Landau equations are used in conjunction with the time-harmonic Helmholtz wave equation to form a general purpose analysis tool for the study of various geometries and HTS materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristic-absorption: a general method to improve absorbing boundary conditions (EM scattering)
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The characteristic-absorption scheme is shown to be successful in reducing the reflection of the first order Mur scheme (1981). It produces a reflection approximately similar to that of the second order scheme in three dimensions. Also, in three dimensions, the corrected first order scheme suffers less from the spurious modes of the second order Mur scheme. The characteristic-absorption technique applied to the first order Mur scheme does not require a special corner treatment, it can be applied in the corners without alteration. Note that this new form of correcting the absorbing boundary condition is not specific to the Yee algorithm and can be applied to other hyperbolic problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: "SPICE" as a Maxwell's equations solver
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper SPICE is used as a tool to model Maxwell's equations in two dimensions. It is shown that the transmission-line equivalent of Maxwell's equations is preferred over the lumped network. The combined fine-coarse cell arrangement may be used to reduce the total number of cells needed and thus improve efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of a loaded cavity with automatic adaptive mesh refinement
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Presents a continuation of the work of Pichon and Bossavit (1993) and Li et al. A brief review of the symmetrical approach to cavity field computations in Pichon and Bossavit is given at first. Such an approach treats both electric and magnetic formulations and obtains an error estimate for adaptive mesh refinement. A similar idea has been presented in Li et al. for the purpose of eddy-current computations, and an automatic mesh refinement software has been realised. The present authors apply the developed model to a microwave cavity problem. A discussion on the choice of mixed (electric + magnetic) error estimators is given as well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristic modal analysis using a Galerkin shell
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The method of characteristic modes is a relatively little used alternative formulation of the method of moments. The paper describes the implementation of a suite of general purpose computer programs for the determination and optimization of characteristics modes for arbitrary structures. The characteristic modes of a number of antenna configurations are then examined. The technique has been found most useful for the design of antenna systems for complex structures, particularly those of vehicles. It is well-known that the characteristics of a particular antenna may be dramatically altered by spurious current flow on the structure on which it is mounted. With characteristic modes however, the antenna and its mounting structure may be considered as one. The determination of its modal set allows the current flow on the complete composite structure to be optimized and hence exploited to beneficial effect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computations of birefringence characteristics of anisotropic fibres by solving the vectorial Maxwell equations
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Presents in detail, a numerical approach for solving the vectorial Maxwell equations that like earlier methods is based on the finite-element method but differs from them primarily in the process used to find the modes of propagation. This procedure can be applied regardless of the geometrical shape of the fibre and is well suited to cases where the propagation media are anisotropic since no spurious modes are generated. Another advantage is convenience of application; the various mathematical steps involved can easily be performed with commercially available software packages. This method uses an iterative numerical procedure in which solutions of the Maxwell equations obtained by scalar approximation are used as trial functions in solving the vectorial Maxwell equations. This process employs a new integral expression that is developed for computing the propagation constant which takes into account the anisotropic properties of the dielectric media.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling the damping of screened room resonances by ferrite tiles using frequency dependent boundaries in TLM
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: A new technique which allows the simulation of thin ferrite absorbing tiles in a coarse TLM mesh is described. Results are presented which show a good fit to manufacturers' reflectivity curves. Experimental and simulation results for a screened room partially lined with ferrite are presented to demonstrate the accuracy of the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient use of symmetry for finite element analysis of eigenvalue problems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Eigenvalue problems have an infinite spectrum of modal solutions with varying symmetry properties. Confusion often arises, especially for structures with a high degree of symmetry, as to the mesh size and boundary conditions required to solve the geometry most effectively. A systematic procedure for the use of symmetry in conjunction with the finite element method is described. Symmetry analysis allows the azimuthal symmetry of the modes, and their degeneracies to be predicted using representation theory of groups. The mesh size, boundary conditions and number of solutions required to calculate all the modes in the waveguide using finite element analysis can then be determined. The procedure is illustrated with some simple examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of spectral domain technique in analysis of multi-layer planar antennas and radiating structures
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper explains a computer technique for accurate and efficient analysis of multi-layer planar antennas fed by planar transmission lines. The technique is based on the electric field integral equation (EFIE) and exploits the Galerkin method in the spectral domain for the moment solution of the equation. Entire domain travelling wave basis functions are used to represent the incident and reflected currents on the feed line, piecewise sinusoidal basis functions are employed to approximate the current in the region of the discontinuity of the feed line with the adjoining metallisation and appropriate basis functions are employed to approximate the currents on the rest of the metallisations. The type of the current expansion on the feed line allows the effects of possible radiation along the feed to be duly accounted for in the computation of the input impedance, radiation patterns etc. The expansion presented can be modified for an approximate analysis. Approximate analyses are important for reducing the computing time, permitting the technique to be usable on personal computers. Results for two examples, a stacked patch antenna fed by a microstrip line and a terminated coplanar strips line, are reported and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Response of coplanar stripline to antenna fields in the near field zone
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper presents a general model for the coupling of antenna fields to lossy striplines when the line is placed in the near-field zone of the antenna and the fields are highly non-uniform. The aim is to develop a general and fast algorithm for the line response which can be applied to any form of transmission lines given the line geometry and model for the antenna fields. Because of the complicated nature of the field distributions the actual coupling field calculations involve complex integrals and numerical procedures are employed to obtain the final results. Several antenna field distributions in different zones are considered and the numerical procedures adopted for the coupled field calculations are given in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space change of eddy current power by induction heating of steel cylinders
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: Finite difference (FDM), finite element (FEM) and integral equation methods are widely used in the numerical simulation of electromagnetic and heat transfer problems of induction heating. Each of these methods has certain advantages and can be used either directly or in combination with others. Both the FDM and FEM discretise a continuous function, and generate simultaneous algebraic equations to be solved for nodal functions. A difficulty that often arises when solving electromagnetic problems is how to treat regions that extend to infinity in space directions. Several methods have been used that take into account the infinite exterior region, all of which have some advantages and some disadvantages. As an alternative to FDM and FEM, the integral equation method (IEM) has been used to solve induction eddy current problems for cylindrical geometries. In contrast with the differential approach the integral equation approach does not require additional boundary conditions. One of the main advantages of the integral equations is that the area of the integration is confined to surfaces. Experience of using different numerical methods for solving induction heating problems shows that the combination of FDM or FEM with IEM is very promising.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The boundary-element-like estimation of the electromagnetic force in the finite element method
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The authors propose the following method. Firstly, they analyze the investigated region only by the finite element method (FEM), after that they locate the hypothetical boundary properly surrounding the points where they desire the values of the magnetic flux density B in the homogeneous region. Finally, they calculate B at inner points by the boundary element method (BEM) using the values obtained by the FEM as the boundary conditions. This method is easily applied to complicated multi-material problems. Calculating B at inner points continuously by the BEM, seems to result in an improvement of the accuracy of the estimation of the electromagnetic force compared with the results obtained only by the FEM. They adopt several physical quantities to this method as unknowns, and also show the propriety and advantage of this method by analyzing a simple model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the FDTD technique on microwave heating
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: The manufacturers rating of the power output of a domestic oven is based on the power delivered to a specified load of water. In fact, the power dissipated in a load can vary considerably with, for example, the mass, the shape or the location of the load. The authors use an enhanced version of the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method to investigate how the power absorbed by the workloads changes with these factors. In microwave heating and drying it is also important to know the field and the temperature distribution in the heated objects. They investigate how the distribution changes when the frequency of the source changes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the use of combined potential sets to cope with general eddy current problems
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the use of the combined (vector and/or scalar) potential sets aimed at dealing with some engineering eddy current problems with lower computing cost. A 3-D eddy current combined code based on the A-V-A- psi and T- psi - psi has been made, and the relevant numerical behaviours of the combined potential sets are shown by the numerical conjugate test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of sensitivity analysis to the calculation of electromagnetic field quantities
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper investigates the application of sensitivity analysis to the calculation of electromagnetic field quantities, such as force. This is particularly important in the design of electrical devices. The electromagnetic field is described by means of a finite element network model which is similar to the classical finite element method. Tellegen's theorem is then applied to the network model to assess the sensitivity analysis. The method is simple requiring only one calculation of the electromagnetic field, for any small perturbation of the system. An algorithm and a 2D magnetostatic problem are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimised image theory for dielectric layer modelling in PCBs
publicationTitle: 1994 Second International Conference on Computation in Electromagnetics
abstract: In the design of PCBs for high frequency applications, it is essential to be able to simulate the electrical behaviour of the PCB layout before it is fabricated to avoid having many expensive design iterations. A powerful CAD tool called FASTERIX is considered. FASTERIX produces an equivalent circuit model for the metallisation and substrate of a PCB. This model is then merged with models for the components attached to the PCB and the combined circuit simulated with a circuit analysis program. Computing the values of the capacitances in the equivalent circuit model of the PCB takes the majority of the CPU time used to generate this circuit in a typical FASTERIX simulation.
